items.title: AstraZeneca, Calidi, Tempest make significant workforce cuts
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Serious adverse events mar robust efficacy data for Helus’ psychedelic in major depression
items.snippet: Helus Pharma's psilocin-based HLP003 significantly reduced symptoms of major depressive disorder in the adjuvant setting in a Phase 3 trial but was tripped up in the stock market by three serious adverse events.

items.title: J&J pays $2.2B upfront for Ollin, taps Blackstone to fund eye disease trial
items.snippet: Blackstone will provide $750 million for Phase 3 development of Ollin Biosciences’ retinal disease bispecific as Johnson & Johnson looks to bolster its eye therapeutics pipeline after several setbacks.

items.title: Lilly’s early-stage M&A quest finds $1.5B deal for Calytrix’s blood cancer work
items.snippet: Eli Lilly's business development team has inked 14 buyouts this year so far, with Calytrix Bio tucking into the pharma’s oncology pipeline.

items.title: FDA’s Summit rejection puts PD-1xVEGF class on notice to establish overall survival
items.snippet: The FDA rejected Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab over the weekend, sending a strong message to rival drugmakers Bristol Myers Squibb, BioNTech, Pfizer, Merck and AbbVie.

items.title: Novo’s CagriSema drives more than 20% weight loss at lower doses
items.snippet: As Novo awaits an FDA decision for its next-gen obesity asset, the company has presented more data at ObesityWeek that could help buoy sentiment on the amylin/GLP-1 combination that disappointed investors a couple of years ago.

items.title: Their loss, our gain? Canada makes its case to Europe amid U.S. instability
items.snippet: Companies at BIO-Europe said shifting U.S. politics have created an opening to promote Canada’s strengths to European partners.

items.title: ObesityWeek 2026: Wave outlines case for body composition–based trial design
items.snippet: Across three cohorts in Wave Life Sciences’ mid-stage trial of WVE-007, higher baseline body mass index and excessive body fat have been associated with a more pronounced effect, Rodman & Renshaw said following the company’s ObesityWeek update.

items.title: Rising costs leave 9 in 10 new medicines unprofitable, IQVIA finds
items.snippet: To achieve a positive return, drugs launched from 2016 to 2020 must generate nearly $12 billion in sales, up from just $1.4 billion for drugs launched in the early 1990s.

items.title: Seawolf surfaces with $100M, $1.2B Sanofi pact for redosable DNA medicines
items.snippet: Backed by Novartis’ venture arm, Eli Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics, Seawolf is advancing its nonviral DNA delivery platform while inking a pact with Sanofi.

items.title: Emerging biotech hubs step up as innovation economics evolve
items.snippet: How India and other emerging hubs for drug development can be key to reshaping medical costs globally.

items.title: BioSpace 40 Under 40 winners Paull, Zhang let patients with rare disease lead the way at BridgeBio
items.snippet: BridgeBio has produced two young leaders on BioSpace’s 2026 40 Under 40 list. Morgan Paull and Christine Zhang attribute their early success to the company’s unique hub-and-spoke model and a drive to help patients with few treatment options. “It’s very personal,” Paull said.

items.title: Alzheimer’s field looks beyond amyloid as biopharma converges at CTAD 2026
items.snippet: This week, biopharma companies including Biogen, Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche are in Boston with new data on their efforts to tackle Alzheimer’s disease.

items.title: Deaths, failed trials and other recent setbacks in the autoimmune space
items.snippet: Novartis, Bristol Myers Squibb, argenx and more have recently been hit with challenges as they attempt to advance assets targeting autoimmune diseases, with some programs being axed entirely while others were set aside for strategic reasons or paused over safety concerns.

items.title: Summit's PD-1xVEGF rejected by FDA in lung cancer
items.snippet: The FDA has denied an approval for Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab to treat EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, blocking the drug’s entry to the U.S. after it became available in China in 2024.

items.title: Cellectis could cut 70% of workforce in shift to in vivo therapies
items.snippet: Cellectis’ business transformation could cost around 160 global employees their jobs. The company has stopped enrollment in its two CAR T programs as it focuses on trials of its in vivo candidates.

items.title: PharmaLogic buys Lantheus plant to build transatlantic radiopharmaceutical CDMO
items.snippet: Less than two years after acquiring the assets, Lantheus is selling its CDMO unit and a New Jersey production plant to PharmaLogic.

items.title: Arrowhead’s Ionis problem, Kyverna’s next-gen end and more biotech earnings
items.snippet: When Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ Tryngolza undersold, investors immediately looked to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ executives for answers on how they will navigate a launch in the same market.

items.title: HHS pumps up to $25M into ibogaine, other psychotropic drugs on Veteran’s Day
items.snippet: Ibogaine, which operates via a “matrix pharmacology,” has long been a focus of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump administration.

items.title: Windward nets $175M IPO, bringing 2026 biotech debuts to 35
items.snippet: Windward Bio’s public debut brings this year’s IPO count well above the sluggish total of eight in 2025.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
